# Complaints and banishment

## In short
- Each citizen can file up to **4 complaints a day** by default. You need at least **20 soul points** and a reason.
- A citizen is **shunned (banished)** once the complaints against them reach **8** (the default threshold).
- If the town has built the Gallows, the Chocolate Cross or the Meat Locker, reaching the threshold **executes** the citizen instead. An already-shunned citizen is executed at **6** complaints.
- Shunned citizens lose their non-essential "impoundable" items to the bank. They cannot attack, devour or (without the Ministry of Slavery) build. Outside town they can hide items in a secret stash.
- When the town falls into chaos or is devastated, every banishment is lifted.

## How it works

### Filing a complaint
You file it from the other citizen's home [1]. The checks, in order:
- **Who can't complain:**
  - You can't complain against yourself.
  - A banished citizen can't file a complaint, but can still withdraw one.
  - An author with fewer than `AntiGriefMinSp` soul points gets an error. The default is **20 SP** [2].
  - Dummy accounts can't complain against real accounts.
- **What you need:**
  - A valid reason is required for any complaint above severity "none".
  - The target must be alive and in your town.
- **Against an already-banished citizen:** a complaint only counts if the town has a finished Gallows `r_dhang_#00`, Chocolate Cross `small_eastercross_#00` or Meat Locker `small_fleshcage_#00`. Without one, you get the message "already banished… only useful if the town builds a gallows or a meat cage."
- **Daily limit:** each new complaint uses the daily `Complaint` action counter. It is refused once the counter reaches `CitizenProperties::ComplaintLimit`, which defaults to **4** [3]. Daily action counters reset at night [4].
- **Severity:** set to Kill (2) if any of the three execution buildings exists, otherwise Banish (1). There are three levels: None 0, Banish 1, Kill 2 [5].
- **One complaint per pair:** each author/culprit pair can only have one complaint [5]. Setting it back to "none" withdraws it.
- **Weight:** a complaint counts **2** if the author has a hero job and People's Court `small_court_#00` is built. Otherwise it counts 1 [1].
- **Notification:** the culprit gets a crow PM when a complaint is added (unless that complaint triggered the banishment) or withdrawn. The PM includes the current complaint count.
- **Privacy:** complaint log entries are visible to admins only [6].

### Banishment or execution (`updateBanishment`)
The check runs after every complaint [7]:
1. Nothing happens if the culprit is dead or the town is in **chaos**.
2. **Threshold:** `OptModifierComplaintsShun` = **8**. For an already-banished culprit it is `OptModifierComplaintsKill` = **6** [8]. An already-banished culprit is ignored unless the town has the Gallows, Chocolate Cross or Meat Locker.
3. **Action:** happens if shunning is enabled (`OptFeatureShun`, default **true**) or one of those buildings exists, **and** the complaints reach the threshold. It also happens if the ban is forced, as in an insurrection.
4. **Execution vs. shunning:** if a Gallows, Chocolate Cross or Meat Locker exists and the ban isn't forced, the citizen is **executed** instead of shunned.
5. **Every action** does the following:
   - removes roles flagged "disallowed for shunned";
   - cancels the citizen's escort and frees anyone they were escorting;
   - moves items to the bank (see below);
   - deletes **all** complaints against the citizen.
6. **Shunning (no execution)** also:
   - sets the banished flag and writes a town log entry;
   - gives the picto `r_ban_#00`;
   - sends a crow PM listing the items taken (there is a special version for insurrections);
   - from **day 3**, adds the citizen's `RevengeItems` to their rucksack (empty by default).
7. **Execution order:**
   - **Chocolate Cross:** death by ChocolateCross. The building is reset to unbuilt (0 AP, 0 HP); the citizens "ate" it.
   - **Gallows:** death by Hanging, logged as public justice. The Gallows is reset to unbuilt [7]. Its card says it works only once and must be rebuilt [9].
   - **Meat Locker** (only if there is no Gallows or Cross): death by FleshCage. The Meat Locker gains **+60 temporary defence if the victim had a hero job, +40 otherwise**. No body is left in the home [7].

### Items taken on banishment (`recoverBanItems`)
- Only **non-essential** items are taken [7].
  - When shunned, only items with the property `impoundable` go.
  - When executed, all of them go.
- Items are taken from the home chest. Rucksack items are only taken if the citizen is **in town** (zone is null).
- Everything goes to the bank, and hidden items are **un-hidden**.

### Hidden stashes
- **Making a stash** [10]:
  - The "hide" option only works as "drop all". It hides every non-essential rucksack item onto the zone floor and costs **2 AP**. With fewer than 2 AP it fails.
  - It only works if the town is in chaos or **no non-banished citizen is in the zone**.
  - Otherwise the items are dropped *visible*, the 2 AP are still spent, and you're told you were watched.
  - On success, the zone records when the items were hidden.
  - Hiding is only valid from rucksack to the local floor [11].
- **Who sees hidden items:** hidden items on a zone floor are shown only to banished viewers or in chaos. Hidden items in your own chest are always shown to you [12].
- **Finding a stash:**
  - A **non-banished** citizen entering a zone with hidden items has a **5%** chance to reveal them all. The discovery is logged [13].
  - A non-banished citizen digging in such a zone also has a **5%** chance to find it ("secret stash… probably made by a banished citizen") [14].
  - In the move code, the "hidden at" time is cleared on the zone variable `$zone` rather than `$new_zone`. That may be the zone the citizen left; I read this from the excerpt but did not confirm it.
- **On death:** hidden items in the dead citizen's home chest become visible [15].
- **Banned Citizen's Note** (`banned_note_#00`): found in the Citizen's Tent ruin (7.9%). Reading it reveals a zone [16]. That zone is the one where items were hidden most recently [17]. A shunned citizen who dies gets such a note in their chest [18].

### Being shunned: restrictions
- No attacking citizens in town [1].
- No devouring in town, even as a ghoul [1].
- No filing complaints [1].
- No construction work unless the Ministry of Slavery is built. Repairs are still allowed [19].
- No taking items from the bank [20].
- The trash search limit is locked at `TrashSearchLimit`, default 3, or +1 for the Scavenger [21].
- They can see hidden stashes on zone floors (see above).

### Insurrection
A banished citizen without status `tg_insurrection` can join the insurrection while progress is below 100 [1].
- Let n = living non-banished citizens and s = living banished citizens.
- Progress added = ceil((5×0.3 + 0.7×5×s/n) × s / 10), or 100 if n = 0.
- Example: s = 3, n = 10 gives ceil((1.5 + 1.05) × 0.3) = ceil(0.765) = 1.
- At 100 or more:
  - complaints against all living citizens are deleted;
  - banished citizens are un-banished and get `tg_revolutionist`;
  - every other living citizen is **force-banished**. That is never an execution, and the insurrection version of the crow PM is used.
- The participant gets `tg_insurrection`.

### Killing citizens
- **Aggression** [22]:
  - Costs `OptModifierAttackAp` AP (default **5**). You must be in the same zone or both in town, and not tired.
  - **Anti-grief protection:** attacks are blocked at no cost if `OptModifierAttackProtect` is on or the attacker has under 20 SP. The block is lifted while any living ghoul is in town.
  - **Attacking a ghoul always kills it** (GhulBeaten), even under protection.
  - An already wounded target can't be attacked, and no AP is spent.
  - Otherwise the target is wounded with chance `OptModifierAttackChance` (default **0.5**). A defender in town gets a crow PM.
  - Aggression never kills a non-ghoul.
  - Outside, attacks are not allowed at 0/0 or against a citizen exploring a ruin [23].
- **Ghoul devouring:**
  - Kills the victim (GhulEaten) and lowers ghoul hunger by 65.
  - In town, the chance of being seen = other living citizens in town / population. Outside, it is always logged [24].
- **Poison:** consuming a deadly-poisoned item kills by Poison [25].
- **Execution** by Gallows, Chocolate Cross or Meat Locker (above).

## What changes it
| Source | Effect |
|---|---|
| People's Court `small_court_#00` (12 AP, blueprint level 3) | Complaints by hero-job authors count 2 [1]. Also +5 bank-take limit [26] |
| Gallows `r_dhang_#00` (13 AP, needs Workshop) | Reaching the threshold hangs the citizen; single use [9] [7] |
| Chocolate Cross `small_eastercross_#00` (13 AP, blueprint level 5) | Same as the Gallows, death by ChocolateCross; it is consumed [27] |
| Meat Locker `small_fleshcage_#00` (40 AP) | Execution if there is no Gallows or Cross; +40 temporary defence (+60 for a hero-job victim); reusable [7] |
| Ministry of Slavery `small_slave_#00` (15 AP, blueprint level 4) | Shunned citizens may build. The AP still needed is multiplied by 2/3 and rounded up, so each AP they invest counts about 1.5× [19] |
| Hero skill Sweet Revenge (`revenge`, legacy, 241 hero days) | 2× poison `poison_#00` if shunned on day 3 or later [28] |
| Reclusive `super_recluse1` / `super_recluse2` (0 / 40 hero days) | Revenge items: 2× `poison_#00`, or 2× `poison_#00` + `infect_poison_#00` [29] [30] |
| Chaos | Complaints have no effect. Hiding always succeeds and everyone sees hidden zone items [7] [10] |
| Settings | `OptFeatureShun` (true), `OptModifierComplaintsShun` (8), `OptModifierComplaintsKill` (6), `ComplaintLimit` (4), `AntiGriefMinSp` (20), `OptModifierAttackAp` (5), `OptModifierAttackChance` (0.5), `OptModifierAttackProtect` (false) |

## Town types
- **Default and remote:** default values. Remote only changes the soul generation coefficient [31].
- **Small:** `citizen_attack.protection` = true, so attacks are blocked unless a ghoul is alive. The `r_ban_#00` picto is awarded instantly there and in the default config [32].
- **Pandemonium (panda):**
  - attacks cost 4 AP and wound with chance 0.6;
  - the Gallows and Meat Locker are unlocked from the start;
  - complaint thresholds are unchanged [33].
- **Custom towns** can change any of the settings above.
- **All towns:** at night, if 1–10 citizens are alive, at least one is in town, and the day is past 3, the town enters chaos and **every banishment is lifted**. Devastation also lifts all banishments [34].

- Where `ChestHiddenStashLimit` (default 0) is used; I found no code using it.
- The bank-take ban, the trash lock and the Banned Citizen's Note behaviour come from summaries only.
